patients.summary: Uninsured construction laborer and groundskeeper with severe alcohol use disorder, untreated chronic hepatitis C, alcoholic cirrhosis and asplenia after a 2013 splenectomy, who joins in 2018. Over the years he develops porphyria cutanea tarda, folate deficiency anemia, vitamin D deficiency with secondary hyperparathyroidism and severe malnutrition, and in July 2026 is hospitalized with alcoholic pancreatitis complicated by withdrawal delirium and ARDS.

orders.reason: Chronic hepatitis C, heavy alcohol use

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
42 y/o man here to set up care. Hasn't had a regular doctor in years. Coworker on a job site recommended us.

HPI: Feels okay overall. Came in mostly because his wife pushed him to, and because he knows he has hep C and has never done anything about it. He was told he had it around the time of his accident in 2013, never followed up. No records available, he doesn't remember where the testing was done.
Drinks every day. Mostly vodka, he estimates close to a bottle a day, beer on weekends on top of that. Has been at this level for well over a decade, started heavy drinking in his mid-20s. No withdrawal seizures that he knows of. Morning shakes some days, settles with a drink. Not interested in treatment today, but willing to talk about it.
Splenectomy 2013 after a car accident (he was the passenger). Was told afterward he should have shots and 'carry antibiotics' and did neither.
No abdominal swelling, no vomiting blood, no black stools, no confusion per his account.

PMH: hep C (untreated), splenectomy 2013.
Meds: none.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father drank heavily and died of liver cirrhosis. Mother has type 2 diabetes. Nobody with blood cancers or porphyria that he knows.
SH: married. Construction laborer, also mows and does groundskeeping part time in the summer. Never smoked. No drugs. No health insurance.

Exam: thin, alert, smells of alcohol, cooperative. No jaundice. No spider angiomata seen. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, well-healed midline scar, liver edge not clearly felt, no fluid wave. No asterixis. Mild fine tremor of outstretched hands. Skin without rash.

A/P:
1. Alcohol use disorder, severe. AUDIT-C 11. Discussed liver risk plainly, he listened. Not ready for detox or a program. Start thiamine 100 mg daily. Will keep raising it.
2. Chronic hepatitis C, reported. Checking antibody and viral load, HBV serologies, HIV. Liver panel, INR, CBC, GGT. Abdominal ultrasound to look at the liver.
3. Asplenia after splenectomy. Penicillin VK 250 mg twice daily for prophylaxis. Starting his vaccines today: PCV13, Hib, MenACWY and MenB first doses, plus Tdap since he can't recall the last one. Polysaccharide pneumococcal in 8 weeks. Told him any fever over 101 means a call to us the same day.
4. Uninsured: front desk to give him the cash price sheet for labs and imaging.

RTC 6 weeks after ultrasound.

documents.title: Vaccine Administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PCV13 L deltoid, Hib R deltoid, MenACWY L deltoid, MenB R deltoid, Tdap L deltoid (separate sites marked). VIS sheets given. Lot numbers in the immunization record. Tolerated, waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: Results Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with results. Hep C antibody reactive and viral load positive at about 1.2 million, so this is active chronic hep C. HBV surface antigen and antibody both negative, so not immune to hep B and will vaccinate. HIV negative. AST higher than ALT, GGT high, platelets a bit low, INR 1.1. Explained these fit liver injury from alcohol plus the virus. Ultrasound is booked for the 24th. He asked what it costs, gave him the front desk number.

reports.text:
EXAM: Ultrasound, complete abdomen.
HISTORY: Chronic hepatitis C, heavy alcohol use.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: Liver: normal size, nodular surface contour with coarse heterogeneous echotexture. No focal hepatic lesion. Main portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. Hepatic veins patent.
Gallbladder: no stones, no wall thickening. No pericholecystic fluid.
Bile ducts: common bile duct 4 mm, not dilated.
Pancreas: visualized portions unremarkable.
Spleen: surgically absent.
Kidneys: right 10.9 cm, left 11.2 cm, normal echogenicity, no hydronephrosis, no stones.
Aorta: normal caliber.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Nodular, coarsened liver consistent with cirrhosis. No focal liver lesion. No ascites. Patent portal vein. Post-splenectomy.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back to go over the ultrasound. Still drinking daily, maybe a little less he says. Has taken the thiamine most days. Penicillin: honest that he took it for about a week and stopped, says he forgets the second dose and doesn't see the point when he feels fine.
No abdominal swelling, no leg swelling, no bleeding, no confusion.

O: BP and pulse as charted. Thin. No jaundice, no ascites on exam, no asterixis.

Ultrasound 4/24: nodular coarse liver c/w cirrhosis, no mass, no ascites, portal vein open. Labs from April reviewed with him again.

A/P:
1. Alcoholic cirrhosis, compensated. Added to problem list. Hep C a second driver. Spent a good part of the visit on what cirrhosis means and why stopping drinking is the single biggest thing. He said he'd think about it.
2. Chronic hep C, confirmed with viral load.
3. Asplenia. Back over why the penicillin matters. MenB #2, hep A #1, hep B #1 today. Nurse visit in 3-4 weeks for the polysaccharide pneumococcal vaccine, MenACWY #2, hep B #2.
4. AUD, severe. Continue thiamine.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before work, still in work boots. PPSV23 L deltoid, MenACWY #2 R deltoid, hep B #2 L deltoid. No reaction to April or May shots per pt besides a sore arm. Next due: hep A #2 and hep B #3 in November. Reminder card given.

documents.title: Fill History
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pulled outside fill history while prepping for August visit. Thiamine filled 4/10 and 6/12. Penicillin VK filled once, 4/10, 30-day supply, not refilled. Flagged for PCP.

documents.title: Missed Visit Outreach
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called re: missed appt yesterday. Pt says a job ran late, apologized. Rebooked for late October, asked for an early slot. Reminded him of the thiamine refill on file.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Rescheduled after August no-show. Busy season over. Drinking unchanged, 'still a bottle most days.' Takes thiamine when he remembers. Penicillin not taking; we talked about it again and he agreed to try to keep the bottle by the coffee maker. No fevers this year. No swelling, no bleeding, no confusion.
O: vitals as charted, weight stable. No jaundice, no ascites, no asterixis. Fine tremor.
A/P:
- Cirrhosis, compensated: CMP, CBC, INR today.
- AUD severe: AUDIT-C 11. Offered referral to an outpatient program, declined for now. Continue thiamine.
- Asplenia: penicillin re-sent. Flu shot today. Hep A #2 and hep B #3 due in late November, nurse visit booked.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver numbers about the same as April. Platelets still mildly low, INR stable. No change in plan. Pt notified by phone, voicemail.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep A #2 R deltoid and hep B #3 L deltoid. Hep A and hep B series now complete. Tolerated well. Asked whether he has been taking the penicillin, he shrugged and said 'some days.' Passed along to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Winter is slow at work so he's had more time on his hands and admits drinking has crept up. Wife is frustrated with him. No jaundice he's noticed, no belly swelling, eating 'one real meal a day.' Thiamine yes, penicillin mostly no.
O: vitals as charted. Thin, no jaundice, no ascites, no asterixis.
A/P:
1. AUD severe, AUDIT-C 12. Long talk. Gave him the number for the regional recovery line and a list of meetings in town. He took the paper.
2. Compensated cirrhosis: labs today.
3. Asplenia: same counseling on penicillin and fever.
4. Eat more regularly, protein with each meal.
RTC 6 months for physical, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gregory, your labs look about like last fall. Liver tests are still elevated in the pattern we see with alcohol, and your platelets are a little low, which fits the cirrhosis. Blood counts otherwise okay, kidneys normal. Nothing urgent. The most helpful thing for these numbers is cutting back on drinking. See you in September.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called for thiamine refill, ran out a couple weeks ago. Sent 90-day supply per standing order. Asked about penicillin, he declined a refill, says he has 'plenty left.'

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM
Working full days, groundskeeping on weekends through the fall. Drinking the same. Mood okay, PHQ-2 1. Sleeps poorly some nights. Thiamine most days. Penicillin: not taking.
ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no abdominal swelling, no blood in stool, no dark stool, no vomiting blood, no fevers.
Exam: thin but steady. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, scar healed, no ascites, liver edge not felt today. No edema. Skin: sun-tanned forearms, no rash. Neuro: fine postural tremor, gait normal.
Health maintenance: vaccines for asplenia and hep A/B complete; MenACWY booster due 2023. Tdap 2018. Flu shot today. Colon screening starts at 45, not yet. HIV screen done 2018.
A/P: compensated alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic hep C, asplenia, severe AUD. Labs today. Same message on alcohol; he isn't ready. RTC 5-6 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from the physical: liver enzymes in his usual range, platelets mildly low, INR 1.2, kidneys and electrolytes normal. Cholesterol fine. Letter mailed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked after the December cancellation (snow job, he said).
S: No new complaints. Drinking daily, unchanged. Thiamine on and off. Penicillin: stopped again. Denies swelling, bleeding, confusion, fevers.
O: vitals as charted. No jaundice, no ascites, mild tremor, no asterixis.
A/P: compensated alcoholic cirrhosis with chronic hep C; severe AUD; asplenia. Labs drawn. Brief intervention again, he can say back the risks but isn't changing. Penicillin re-sent with a pill box from the nurse. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs stable from fall. No changes. Called, left message with results.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his truck after work, connection poor at times. Identity confirmed with DOB.
Still working, crews kept going through the shutdown. No cough, no fever. Drinking the same or a bit more with the evenings at home. No belly swelling, no yellow eyes, no black stools.
No vitals today.
Plan: continue thiamine. Labs deferred until he can come in. Reviewed fever plan with asplenia: any temp over 101 means call right away, day or night. In-person in late summer.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First in-person since February. Missed August video. Things are tense at home, he and his wife 'aren't doing great.' Drinking more, he thinks. Appetite poor, mostly eats on the job site. No fevers, no bleeding, no swelling.
PHQ-2 2, says he's stressed rather than down.
O: vitals as charted, weight down a little. No jaundice, no ascites. Tremor.
A/P:
- AUD severe, worse with stress at home. AUDIT-C 12. Offered counseling referral and a program, declined. Continue thiamine.
- Cirrhosis compensated, hep C: labs.
- Asplenia: flu shot today. Not taking penicillin.
- Colon screening: turns 45 next month, will start with FIT in the spring.
RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver tests a little higher than spring, otherwise stable. Platelets in the 140s. Reviewed with pt by phone; he knows the drinking drives it.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: He and his wife are divorcing, he moved into a rental in Florence in January. Says it's 'for the best' but he is drinking more since, most nights more than a bottle. Working. No fevers, no swelling, no bleeding, no confusion. COVID vaccine: plans to get it at the pharmacy next month.
O: weight 65 kg, down 2 kg from when he joined. No jaundice, no ascites, tremor.
A/P:
1. AUD severe, heavier with the divorce. Offered counseling, a program, and to talk about a medicine for cravings; he wants to 'handle it himself.' Door left open.
2. Cirrhosis, hep C: labs today.
3. Asplenia: same counseling. Penicillin on list, not taking.
4. Weight: eat with protein daily, thiamine.
5. FIT kit next visit.
RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs: same pattern, AST above ALT, albumin holding. Platelets lower this time at 96; recheck next visit. Portal message sent.

documents.body: got both covid shots at the pharmacy april 6 and may 4. picture of the card attached. second one knocked me out for a day.

documents.title: RE: covid shots
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Gregory, both doses are now in your record. See you on the 25th.

orders.reason: Blistering lesions on backs of hands after sun

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: For a few months now, blisters on the backs of both hands and up onto the forearms. They hurt, show up after a day in the sun or if he knocks his hand on something, and take weeks to heal. Thinks it's from work gloves or chemicals at the grounds job. No new soaps. No mouth sores. No joint pain.
Still drinking heavily since the divorce.
O: dorsal hands with a few crusted erosions and two intact tense blisters, scattered pink scars and darker patches. Forearms similar but milder. Rest of the skin clear.
A/P:
1. Blistering eruption on sun-exposed hands. With hep C and heavy drinking I worry about a porphyria picture. Referring to dermatology for evaluation. Gloves and long sleeves outdoors, sunscreen on the backs of the hands.
2. AUD severe: same discussion.
3. Colorectal screening: FIT kit given with instructions.
RTC after derm.

documents.title: FIT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in a couple of years. Portal message sent.

medications.reason: Porphyria cutanea tarda; patient has not started it

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 07/12/2021
Re: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975
Referred by: primary care physician

Thank you for sending Mr. Kearney. He is a 45-year-old man with several months of painful blisters on the dorsal hands and forearms. New lesions come up after sun exposure or small bumps, heal slowly over weeks, and leave fragile skin with darker marks. He works outdoors as a laborer and groundskeeper.

History: chronic hepatitis C, never treated; heavy daily alcohol use; splenectomy after a car accident about eight years ago.
Medications per patient: thiamine; penicillin VK, which he admits he does not take.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with alcohol-related cirrhosis; mother with type 2 diabetes; no known porphyria or blood cancers.

Exam: multiple vesicles and bullae over the dorsal hands and distal forearms with crusted erosions, atrophic scars, milia and patchy hyperpigmentation. Face and trunk spared. Abdomen: the liver edge is palpable about 2 cm below the right costal margin.

Labs today: AST 96, ALT 71. Ferritin 812 ng/mL. HCV RNA detected. Urine total porphyrins 1,460 mcg/g creatinine (elevated).

Impression: porphyria cutanea tarda, in the setting of hepatitis C, heavy alcohol use and iron overload by ferritin.

Plan:
- Low-dose hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice weekly; prescription given.
- Strict sun protection: gloves, long sleeves, broad-spectrum sunscreen, no tanning.
- Stopping alcohol is essential to control this.
- His hepatitis C should be addressed through his primary care physician.
- Follow up here in about 6 months.

Allergies: NKDA.

Thank you for this referral.
Dermatology

documents.title: Patient Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called asking whether we got the skin doctor's note. We have not. He says he saw them July 12, they said it's a liver-related skin condition and gave him a pill to take twice a week. He has not filled it yet, wanted to know if it's 'safe with his liver.' Told him we'd request the consult letter and the PCP will call once we have it. Records request sent to the dermatology office.

documents.title: Records Received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dermatology consultation from 7/12/2021 received by fax after second request. Scanned and routed to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Dermatology letter finally came in August, reviewed. He has porphyria cutanea tarda. He never filled the hydroxychloroquine. Hands a little better since he started wearing gloves at work, still gets new blisters.
Drinking the same, living alone now.
O: vitals as charted. Dorsal hands with healing erosions and scars, no infection.
A/P:
1. PCT per dermatology. Low-dose hydroxychloroquine is reasonable with his liver at that dose, told him so; he says he'll fill it. Sun protection. Stopping alcohol is the main lever.
2. AUD severe: declined referral again.
3. Cirrhosis, hep C: labs next visit.
4. Flu shot today.
RTC 3 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Macrocytic anemia with low white count

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About six weeks of being wiped out, winded on a flight of stairs or carrying lumber, and his tongue is sore and burns with hot coffee. No chest pain. No black stools or blood. Eating poorly, drinking heavily.
O: pale. Tongue red and smooth. Heart regular, soft systolic murmur. Lungs clear. No ascites.
CBC today: hemoglobin just under 9 with MCV about 111 and a low white count.
A/P:
1. Macrocytic anemia, new, with symptoms. Alcohol and nutrition are the likely story but given the low white count and asplenia I'd like hematology to see him. Urgent referral placed. Return sooner if chest pain or worse breathlessness.
2. AUD severe, cirrhosis: unchanged.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - NEW CONSULT
Date of service: 01/06/2022
Patient: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975
Reason for referral: macrocytic anemia, low WBC

HPI: 46-year-old man referred by his PCP. For about two months he has been increasingly tired and short of breath with exertion, and his tongue has been sore. He says his drinking has gone up over the last year since his divorce. No tobacco, no drugs. He tells me he is not actually taking any of his prescribed medicines right now.

PMH: alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis C (untreated), porphyria cutanea tarda (dermatology 2021), splenectomy after MVA ~2013.
Meds (prescribed, not taking): thiamine, penicillin VK, hydroxychloroquine.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis, mother T2DM. No hematologic malignancy.

Exam: pale, mild scleral icterus. Tongue smooth and beefy red. Grade 2/6 systolic flow murmur at the left sternal border. Lungs clear. No lymphadenopathy. Abdomen without ascites.

Data: Hgb 9.2 g/dL, MCV 110 fL, WBC 3.8, platelets 150. Serum folate 2 ng/mL (low). B12 400 pg/mL (normal). AST and ALT mildly elevated.

Assessment: macrocytic anemia due to folate deficiency, from poor intake and heavy alcohol use, with mild leukopenia and low-normal platelets in a patient with cirrhosis.

Plan:
1. Folic acid 1 mg daily, sent to his pharmacy.
2. Diet and alcohol counseling given.
3. Thiamine should be resumed.
4. Repeat CBC with PCP in 4-6 weeks; we are glad to see him again if counts do not recover.

Thank you for the referral.
Hematology & Oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Hematology letter reviewed: folate deficiency anemia, folate 2, B12 fine. On folic acid daily since early January, actually taking it, and restarted thiamine. Tongue better, less winded. Drinking unchanged.
O: less pale. Tongue normal. Soft flow murmur still there. No ascites.
CBC today: hemoglobin up into the 11s; MCV still large, which lags behind.
A/P:
1. Folate deficiency anemia, responding. Continue folic acid 1 mg daily. CBC in a few months.
2. AUD severe: counseled; declined.
3. Penicillin: still not taking it. Re-sent.
RTC 3 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Vitamin D deficiency with elevated PTH

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Still tired even with the blood count better. Hard to focus at work, forgets measurements. Cramps in both calves and thighs most nights. Says he eats plenty of canned fish and milk so 'it can't be calcium.' Folic acid most days.
O: vitals as charted. Mild weakness getting up from a squat. No ascites, no jaundice.
A/P:
1. Fatigue, cramps, proximal weakness in a man with cirrhosis and poor intake. Checking calcium, phosphorus, vitamin D, PTH, CMP, CBC.
2. Folate deficiency anemia: CBC.
3. AUD: same.
Will call with results.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 25-OH vitamin D 9, very low. PTH 112, high. Calcium 8.5, phosphorus 2.6, both low-normal to low. Alk phos up a bit. Pattern fits vitamin D deficiency with a secondary PTH rise; liver disease and diet likely. Given the PTH and his bones, referring to endocrinology rather than just dosing on my own. Hemoglobin holding in the 11s.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gregory, your vitamin D is very low and your parathyroid hormone, which controls calcium, is running high to make up for it. That can explain the cramps, weakness and tiredness. I'm sending you to endocrinology to sort out the right treatment. They will call you to schedule. Your blood count is holding steady.

documents.title: RE: Your Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok. is it going to cost a lot, i dont have insurance

documents.title: RE: Your Lab Results
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Gregory, the endocrinology office offers a self-pay rate and a payment plan. Their number is on the referral paperwork we mailed you.

conditions.label: Secondary hyperparathyroidism
conditions.note: Due to vitamin D deficiency with alcoholic liver disease

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule (2000 units) by mouth daily

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 07/05/2022
Patient: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975
Referring: primary care

Reason: low vitamin D, elevated PTH.

HPI: 46-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis, porphyria cutanea tarda and folate deficiency anemia who has had ongoing tiredness, trouble concentrating and frequent cramps in his legs. He eats a lot of canned salmon, sardines and fortified dairy and was surprised his calcium axis could be off. He works construction and grounds jobs outside nearly every day and does not wear sunscreen. Drinks about a bottle of vodka a day. No recent illness, infection or injury.

Meds: folic acid 1 mg daily, thiamine 100 mg daily; penicillin VK and hydroxychloroquine prescribed but not being taken.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: thin. Strength 4+/5 in hip flexors bilaterally, otherwise full. Reflexes and sensation normal. Thyroid normal. Rest of exam unremarkable.

Labs (5/10/2022, PCP): 25-OH D 9 ng/mL, intact PTH 112 pg/mL, calcium 8.5 mg/dL, phosphorus 2.6 mg/dL.

Assessment: vitamin D deficiency with secondary hyperparathyroidism, in the setting of alcoholic liver disease (reduced hepatic hydroxylation and poor absorption from heavy drinking). His sun exposure does not protect him here. Symptoms of fatigue, cramps and mild proximal weakness fit.

Plan:
1. Cholecalciferol 2000 units daily.
2. Continue dietary calcium as he is doing.
3. Repeat 25-OH D, PTH, calcium and phosphorus in about 4 months through his PCP.
4. Alcohol cessation strongly advised.
No routine follow-up needed here unless PTH stays high once vitamin D is replete.

Endocrinology

conditions.label: Severe malnutrition with multiple micronutrient deficiencies

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Endocrinology letter reviewed: vitamin D deficiency with secondary hyperparathyroidism from his liver disease, started on D3 2000 units daily. He has been taking it with the folic acid in the mornings. Cramps a little less. Still drinking a bottle most days. One meal a day plus snacks.
O: weight 62 kg, down from 67 when he joined. Temporal wasting. No jaundice, no ascites.
A/P:
1. Severe malnutrition with multiple micronutrient deficiencies: folate and vitamin D deficient, albumin falling, steady weight loss, all driven by heavy drinking and poor intake. Added to problem list. Talked through cheap protein: eggs, peanut butter, canned fish, milk. Continue folic acid, thiamine, D3.
2. Vitamin D deficiency / secondary hyperparathyroidism: recheck labs in November as endocrine asked.
3. Cirrhosis, hep C: labs today.
4. AUD severe: AUDIT-C 12, declined referral.
RTC 3 months with labs.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Albumin 3.3, lower than when he joined. Hemoglobin about 12 on folic acid. INR stable. Messaged pt to keep up the folic acid and protein.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid, bivalent COVID booster R deltoid. Tolerated. He asked to have the November lab draw the same day as his visit to save a trip; scheduled.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vitamin D up into the low 20s on 2000 units, PTH coming down toward normal, calcium and phosphorus normal. Going the right way. Keep D3 at the same dose. He did not come for the office visit he'd planned the same morning, only the lab; front desk to rebook.

medications.reason: Patient stopped taking it months ago

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First visit since August (missed the November slot). He went back to dermatology in January on his own: hands had been worse through the fall, new blisters on the backs of both hands, and his urine has been dark like tea for several weeks. No belly pain, no numbness or weakness. They told him the skin condition is acting up, his liver tests were high again, and to start the hydroxychloroquine and quit drinking. He still has not started it. We never got a note from that visit.
Med review with his bottles: taking thiamine and the D3 most days. Folic acid ran out before Christmas and he didn't refill it. Penicillin not taking.
O: vitals as charted. Dorsal hands with erosions, fragile skin and dark patches. No jaundice, no ascites.
A/P:
1. PCT, flaring per his account. Encouraged him to start the hydroxychloroquine, gloves and sleeves. Requesting the January dermatology note.
2. Folic acid: not taking for months; off the list. CBC today, will restart if the anemia is back.
3. Vitamin D: continue D3.
4. Asplenia: MenACWY booster today (5 years from the 2018 series).
5. Colon screening: FIT kit.
6. AUD severe: AUDIT-C 12.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Requested January 2023 dermatology office note by fax. Office said they would send it.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Two months of steadily worse tiredness; can't keep up on the crew. Lightheaded at times when he stands up quickly or climbs a ladder, and his heart races with light work. Similar run-down spells last year with the anemia and then the vitamin D. No blood in stool, no black stool, no vomiting blood, no recent illness. Not following any diet. Says beer most days on top of the liquor.
Still off folic acid.
O: vitals as charted. Pale. No scleral icterus. No lymph nodes in the neck, axillae or groin. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly or splenomegaly felt (post-splenectomy), no ascites. Neuro nonfocal.
CBC today: hemoglobin 9.1, MCV 108. Reticulocyte count 0.4%, low. Smear sent.
A/P:
1. Macrocytic anemia with a low retic, recurrent, off folate for over six months while drinking heavily: most likely recurrent folate deficiency anemia. Restart folic acid 1 mg daily. Smear to look for anything else. Recheck CBC in 6-8 weeks; back to hematology if not recovering.
2. Symptoms: no syncope; ok to keep working but no ladders until the count is up.
3. AUD severe: same talk, harder this time about where this is heading. He listened.
RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Blood smear result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gregory, the blood smear shows large red cells, which fits folate deficiency, and small fragments inside some red cells called Howell-Jolly bodies that are expected in anyone without a spleen. Nothing to suggest a blood cancer. Please take the folic acid every day and come back in about 6 weeks for a recheck.

2. AUD severe, AUDIT-C 11. Offered referral again; not yet.
3. Flu and updated COVID today.
RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 07/08/2024
Patient: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975

Mr. Kearney is 48 and was seen here in 2022 for folate deficiency anemia. He called to come back on his own because he has kept getting sick with infections over the past several months, bruises easily, and has lost about 10 kg over six months without trying. Splenectomy after a car accident roughly a decade ago. He admits he rarely takes his penicillin.

Meds as reported: folic acid 1 mg daily, thiamine 100 mg daily, cholecalciferol 2000 units daily, penicillin VK 250 mg twice daily (rarely taken), hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice weekly (never started).
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: heavy daily alcohol use continues.

Exam: afebrile. Pale. Multiple ecchymoses of varying age on the arms and legs. Abdomen soft and unremarkable, no hepatosplenomegaly. No lymphadenopathy.

Labs: Hgb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 92 fL, WBC 3.2, platelets 120. Peripheral smear: Howell-Jolly bodies.

Assessment:
1. Asplenia with overwhelming post-splenectomy infection risk, heightened by alcohol use, cirrhosis, malnutrition, low white count and non-adherence to prophylaxis.
2. Anemia with leukopenia and mild thrombocytopenia in the setting of alcohol use and cirrhosis; the smear changes are those of asplenia.

Plan:
- Long discussion about OPSI: fever or shaking chills means same-day emergency care, not waiting it out.
- Take penicillin VK 250 mg twice daily every day.
- Keep post-splenectomy vaccines current with his PCP; a pneumococcal update is due.
- Continue folic acid and thiamine.
- PCP to follow counts; we are available as needed.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First visit here in almost a year (missed February, cancelled May). Hematology letter from 7/8 reviewed: OPSI risk, Howell-Jolly bodies, counts down. He went to them himself after a rough winter and spring of being sick on and off. He never came here for those. Lost weight, pants falling off. Drinking daily. Taking folic acid and D3 most days. Penicillin: he has the bottle, 'trying.'
O: weight 53 kg. Thin with muscle wasting. Several bruises on the forearms and shins. No jaundice, no ascites. Lungs clear.
A/P:
1. Asplenia with OPSI risk, per hematology. PCV20 today as they suggested; MenACWY was boosted 2023. Penicillin VK re-sent, same dose. Went over the fever plan again, wrote it on a card for his wallet: fever or chills, call us and go to the ED.
2. Severe malnutrition: weight now 53 kg. Same food plan; he says money is tight. Gave the list of local food pantries.
3. Folate deficiency anemia, cytopenias: counts as per hematology; CBC next visit.
4. Cirrhosis, hep C: CMP, INR today.
5. AUD severe: AUDIT-C 12. Declined referral.
RTC 3 months, I'd like to see him more often.

ANNUAL EXAM
Lives alone in his rental. Working construction and grounds through the fall. Drinking every day, roughly a bottle. Former wife still checks on him now and then. PHQ-9 6: tired, sleeps badly, not hopeless, no thoughts of self-harm.
Meds: folic acid, thiamine, D3 daily; penicillin VK on and off; hydroxychloroquine never started.
ROS: no fevers, no chest pain, no breathlessness, no belly swelling, no black stools, no vomiting blood, no confusion.
Exam: thin, weight steady around 55 kg. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur today. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, midline scar, no ascites. Hands with scarring and darker patches. No edema. Fine tremor, gait steady.
Health maintenance: FIT negative July. Asplenia vaccines: PCV20 2024, MenACWY 2023 (next 2028), MenB and Hib done. Hep A/B series done. Tdap 2018. Flu and COVID at the October nurse visit.
A/P: problems unchanged. Labs today incl. vitamin D and PTH. Same counseling. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - CONSULTATION-LIAISON PSYCHIATRY
Date of service: 07/21/2026
Patient: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975
Requested by: medicine team
Reason: acute confusion and agitation

HPI: 50-year-old man admitted 3 days ago with acute pancreatitis. Background of severe alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis C, asplenia, porphyria cutanea tarda and nutritional deficiencies. Over the last day nursing found him more and more restless and irritable. This morning his former wife, visiting, found him confused and shaking and called the nurse. He is now seeing snakes on the floor of the room. She gives a history of about 25 years of heavy daily drinking; he has had nothing to drink since he came in.

Meds prior to admission: folic acid, thiamine, cholecalciferol, penicillin VK (inconsistent); hydroxychloroquine prescribed, never taken.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals at time of consult: T 38.2 C, BP 162/98, HR 126, RR 24.

Mental status: disoriented to time and place, oriented to self. Frightened, hypervigilant, pulling at his IV lines. Visual hallucinations. Diaphoretic with fine tremor of the hands. Heart and lungs otherwise unremarkable; neurologic exam otherwise nonfocal.

Assessment: alcohol withdrawal delirium, onset roughly 72 hours after his last drink.

Recommendations:
1. Symptom-triggered withdrawal treatment per the primary team's protocol, with close monitoring.
2. One-to-one sitter; frequent reorientation, lights on by day and dim at night, family at bedside when possible.
3. Continue thiamine supplementation.
4. Avoid restraints if at all possible.
5. Addiction medicine follow-up after discharge; he will need a plan for his drinking.
We will follow.

Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry

documents.title: ICU Transfer Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - MEDICAL ICU TRANSFER / ADMISSION NOTE
Date of service: 07/21/2026
Patient: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975

Reason for ICU: hypoxemic respiratory failure.

HPI: 50-year-old man with severe alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis, asplenia, porphyria cutanea tarda and malnutrition, admitted from our ED on 7/18 with acute pancreatitis after two days of severe epigastric pain boring into his back and repeated vomiting, taking little by mouth. On hospital day 3 he developed alcohol withdrawal delirium (psychiatry seen this morning) and this afternoon became acutely short of breath on the floor. He was put on supplemental oxygen with little change in his saturation. He was transferred to the ICU.

Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals on transfer: T 38.3 C, HR 112, RR 32, BP 100/62, SpO2 83% on room air.

Exam: tachypneic and in visible distress, using accessory muscles. Diffuse bilateral crackles. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen with epigastric tenderness and guarding.

Data: glucose 236 mg/dL (elevated). Calcium 7.1 mg/dL (low). ABG on FiO2 0.60: PaO2 55 mmHg. Portable chest x-ray: bilateral patchy opacities. Bedside echo: normal LV function, no pericardial effusion. ECG: no acute changes.

Course in the first hours: aggressive IV fluid resuscitation and supportive care continued; oxygenation did not improve and he was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation.

Assessment:
1. Acute respiratory distress syndrome with refractory hypoxemia. With normal LV function, no effusion and an unremarkable ECG, a cardiac cause is excluded; this is lung injury from his systemic illness, the acute pancreatitis.
2. Acute alcoholic pancreatitis.
3. Alcohol withdrawal delirium.
4. Asplenia, cirrhosis, malnutrition.

Plan: lung-protective ventilation, supportive care for pancreatitis, withdrawal management with psychiatry following, nutrition consult.

Medical Intensive Care Unit
